title: Clinical Specimen Processing Workflow

references.label: Biosafety in Microbiological and Biomedical Laboratories (BMBL)

purpose: To triage, plate, and process a clinical specimen (any body-source specimen submitted for culture) in a way appropriate to its source, so that clinically significant organisms are recovered and reported while the underlying general microbiology techniques (streaking, media selection) reuse the laboratory's existing foundation.
principle: Clinical specimen processing applies the general microbiological techniques already covered (streak plate, selective/differential media) to a clinical context, where the goal shifts from pure-culture isolation of a known organism toward recovering, differentiating, and identifying whichever organism(s) are clinically significant from a mixed, often non-sterile, source — while distinguishing true pathogens from normal flora/contaminants (see the related concept).
requiredMaterials: Appropriate selective/differential/enrichment media for the specimen source
requiredReagents: Gram stain reagents for direct smear, where indicated

procedure.instruction: Confirm specimen acceptability (labeling, appropriate container/transport medium, timing) before processing; reject per the laboratory's specimen rejection criteria if not met.

Select media appropriate to the specimen source and clinical question (e.g. blood agar for general growth, MacConkey for Gram-negative differentiation, plus source-specific media as indicated) — reusing the laboratory's existing general/selective media, not a separate clinical set.

procedure.note: A direct smear result is preliminary and must be correlated with culture, not reported as a final identification on its own.
procedure.instruction: Perform a direct Gram stain on the specimen where clinically indicated (e.g. many normally sterile-site specimens), which can provide same-day preliminary information ahead of culture growth.
Inoculate plates using standard streak technique to obtain isolated colonies; incubate under the atmosphere/temperature appropriate to the suspected organisms and specimen source.

Examine plates at the appropriate interval(s), assess growth against expected normal flora for that specimen source, and proceed to identification/susceptibility testing for organisms judged clinically significant.

observations: Document growth pattern, colony morphology/quantity relative to expected flora for the source, and any organisms warranting further workup.
interpretation: Growth must be interpreted against what is normal/expected flora for the specimen source — the same organism can be a true pathogen from a normally sterile site or an unremarkable contaminant/commensal from a non-sterile site.
precautions: Process specimens promptly to avoid overgrowth of contaminants or die-off of fastidious pathogens.
Follow the biosafety level and containment appropriate to the suspected organism(s), not a single fixed level for all clinical specimens.
limitations: Culture-based recovery can be affected by prior antibiotic therapy, transport delay, or fastidious/slow-growing organisms not recovered by standard media/conditions.
biosafetyNotes: Handle all clinical specimens as potentially containing pathogens of unknown risk group until ruled out; use a biosafety cabinet for aerosol-generating steps and follow standard/universal precautions throughout.
